hardware.variant: One R4 LittleFS network-appliance kit with a 480 x 480 CO5300 display and CST92xx touch controller.

inputs.name: RV32 ILP32 soft-float ELF tested from tmpfs
inputs.revision: Input adapter before the backward wall-clock adjustment regression fix

inputs.name: Published reference build, compiled after the hardware observation

scenario: Launch from tmpfs over SSH. Center the 320 x 480 compiled upstream scene at x=80 on wsdisplay. Open a temporary wsmouse0 device node (character 212:0, mode 0600) for the attached controller. Observe physical contact, release and drag.
expected: A finger press reaches the red MouseArea and moving a finger with a grab on the blue rectangle changes its position within the bounds declared in QML.
observed: The app presented the initial frame and received physical DOWN/UP events. The original red area logged Entered, Pressed (LeftButton shift=false), Exited (pressed=true) when moving outside during contact, and Exited (pressed=false) after a release. The blue rectangle moved from (190,10) to (194,61), (200,89) and (182,166). The operator confirmed the app worked.
limits: The R4 image omitted /dev/wsmouse0. This run used the existing driver through a tmpfs node and did not change NOR or startup configuration.
Click, hold and double-click labels were compared with independent Qt Quick on the host. The on-device QML log covers entered, pressed and exited.
The later adapter revision bounds stale input timestamps after a backward wall-clock change. Its RV32 build and host regression passed; the measured hardware ELF is the first binary listed.
